gen-dafont-bloody-gf-pathway-extreme: Pathway Extreme rounds its letters with clear openings, stubby ascenders and descenders hugging a big x-height, beneath the heading Bloody. Those big round bowls up top are the loudest thing here.
gen-dafont-bloody-gf-preahvihear: Commanding round bowls in Bloody sit over Preahvihear, whose open letter mouths and lofty x-height feel modern and contemporary. That gap between loud heading and open body is the draw.
gen-dafont-bloody-gf-prompt: Approachable and easily readable, Prompt gives its small letters an oversized look and open apertures beneath Bloody. But Bloody commands attention with big round bowls, while Prompt does the quiet work of being read.
gen-dafont-bloody-gf-pt-sans-caption: Bloody arrives with big round bowls and a commanding streak. PT Sans Caption does the other job, with big-bodied lowercase and unclosed bowls that keep a line inviting and contemporary.
gen-dafont-bloody-gf-puritan: Clean rounded forms define Puritan, under Bloody. Its oversized e and a counters stay open to the side, so a full page of text should read smoothly without strain.
gen-dafont-bloody-gf-questrial: Flat, stencil-cut look: Questrial keeps single-weight strokes and a tall band of letters under the round-bowled Bloody. Long text should flow steadily, each o a ring with a constant wall.
gen-dafont-bloody-gf-radio-canada: Loud round bowls, then a steady line: Bloody brings low modulation while the body keeps none. Radio Canada does its best work in tall, full c, s and z, with a clear opening at each curve's end.
gen-dafont-bloody-gf-radio-canada-big: Bloody commands with big round bowls, loud and unmistakable. Radio Canada Big works quieter, a monoline skeleton with an x-height that fills the line and terminals that stop well short of the stem.
gen-dafont-bloody-gf-readex-pro: Readex Pro reads with an unvarying weight from word to word. Broad gaps at the terminals and a marker-like line keep paragraphs moving smoothly, a sober counterweight to Bloody.
gen-dafont-bloody-gf-roboto: Bloody throws down big round lowercase bowls and a commanding attitude. Roboto, clean and contemporary, gives round letters generous mouths and little height contrast between capitals and body, so a stretch of text moves along without snagging.
